proposals.expected_signal: Higher NDCG@10 if reducing dominance of high-degree users/items improves top-rank personalization under frozen full-sort evaluation.
proposals.failure_mode: If popularity bias is already beneficial in ML-1M, degree tempering can suppress useful signal and lower recall on head items.
proposals.hypothesis: Applying degree-tempered edge normalization in light graph propagation will preserve collaborative connectivity while reducing over-smoothing toward popular nodes, improving top-10 ranking precision.

proposals.expected_signal: Higher NDCG@10 if a lightweight gated message transform can separate helpful neighbor evidence from noisy interactions better than pure linear propagation.
proposals.failure_mode: Extra transform capacity may overfit the small interaction graph or destabilize optimization, yielding worse ranking than simpler propagation.
proposals.hypothesis: Replacing fixed neighbor aggregation with a residual gated message transform will let the model learn when to pass through versus attenuate neighbor messages, improving discriminative item ranking.

proposals.expected_signal: Higher NDCG@10 if structured regularization on user/item embeddings reduces memorization and improves generalization of top-ranked items.
proposals.failure_mode: If the base latent factor model is already capacity-limited, dropout can underfit and reduce separability between positives and negatives.
proposals.hypothesis: Injecting embedding-level dropout during pairwise ranking training will regularize co-adapted latent dimensions and improve robustness of the learned ranking function.

proposals.expected_signal: Higher NDCG@10 if a contrastive auxiliary loss makes user/item representations more stable across perturbed graph views without harming the ranking objective.
proposals.failure_mode: Auxiliary contrastive pressure may conflict with pairwise ranking and collapse useful fine-grained distinctions needed for top-10 ordering.
proposals.hypothesis: Augmenting LightGCN with a contrastive auxiliary objective over lightly perturbed graph views will improve representation consistency and reduce sensitivity to sparse neighborhood noise.
